clue.text: Fish caught are storm tossed – here's a bony old one

indicators.note: something tossed about is thrown into disorder, so the preceding words are rearranged
a thing caught is held inside something else, here inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: a common food fish
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An old fish turns up after a storm-tossed catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like the fisherman's verb, but it is the signal for putting one piece inside another. 'One' points back to 'Fish', so the definition is an old bony fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracoderms are extinct jawless fishes of the Palaeozoic era, armoured with bony plates.

clue.text: Spar, tip fixed with one pa cleared

indicators.note: something fixed has been repaired or rigged, so the letters are put into a new order
when something is cleared it is taken away, so those letters go

blocks.note: taken as written
'one' points back to the spar just named, so the word spar itself is used
taken as written; these letters are removed from the spar

explanation.surface: Instructions for rigging a spar: fix its tip and clear away some part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' refers back to 'Spar': SPAR loses PA to leave SR, and TIP plus SR is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprit is a small spar running diagonally across a fore-and-aft sail to extend its peak.

clue.text: To wit, a foul suffering stopped by touch of ruler?

definitions.text: To wit, a foul suffering stopped by touch of ruler?

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, damaged, so the letters before it are disordered
a gap stopped by something has that thing plugged into it

blocks.note: SC is short for scilicet, Latin for 'namely' or 'to wit'
taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the first letter, the 'touch', of this word

explanation.surface: A nasty disease cured by a monarch laying on hands.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: scrofula was the King's Evil, believed cured by the royal touch. R goes in front of the rearranged A FOUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrofula, tuberculosis of the neck glands, was historically called the King's Evil because the monarch's touch supposedly healed it.

clue.text: Chief place occupied by prince from the south

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the south means reading upward, so the word runs backwards
a place occupied by someone has that person inside it

blocks.note: PL is the standard abbreviation for place
an amir or emir is a Muslim prince or ruler

explanation.surface: The main residence is home to a royal visitor from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal can mean first in importance, principal, a fair synonym for chief.

clue.text: One walking slowly up to give a summary

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is written bottom to top

blocks.note: a pacer is a person or horse that walks at a steady pace

explanation.surface: A slow walker summarises the route.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap, short for recapitulate, is to restate the main points briefly.

clue.text: Lecture, mostly bombastic, on stimulant leaves (6, two words)

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word's final letter is dropped

blocks.note: tall, as in tall talk, means exaggerated or bombastic; shortened
kat or khat is a shrub whose leaves are chewed as a stimulant

explanation.surface: A pompous talk delivered by someone high on chewed leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk at someone is to harangue them without listening, which is to lecture them.

clue.text: I provide the wherewithal and pass round wad I cobbled together

indicators.note: something cobbled together is assembled roughly, so the letters are rearranged
one thing going round another encloses it

blocks.note: the Brenner Pass is the Alpine crossing between Austria and Italy
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who earns the money brings a wad of cash home after crossing a pass.
explanation.walkthrough: The specific pass needed is the Brenner, which opens to take the rearranged WAD I after BRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadwinner earns the household income, so providing the means of living.

clue.text: One at special ball is briefly entertained by old poet

indicators.note: briefly means in shortened form, so the word is cut down
a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so it goes inside

blocks.note: maker (makar) is an old, chiefly Scots, word for a poet
is shortened to 's

explanation.surface: A dancer at a ball is hosted by an elderly poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A masker wears a mask, as everyone does at a masquerade, a ball of a special kind.

clue.text: Small Canadian bottle from among ceramic kinds

indicators.note: taking letters from among some words means they lie inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A little bottle sits among assorted pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: A mickey or mick is Canadian slang for a small bottle of spirits, about 375 ml.
explanation.definitionFit: In Canada a mick, short for mickey, is a pocket-sized flask-shaped bottle of liquor.

clue.text: Old spear, certainly not for some Ghanaians

blocks.note: spears were made from ash wood, so ash was an old word for a spear
being anti something is certainly not being for it

explanation.surface: Some Ghanaians reject the old spear outright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Certainly not for' reads as one phrase, but 'for' attaches to the definition; 'certainly not' gives the word meaning against.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashanti are a people of central Ghana, so they are some of the country's inhabitants.

clue.text: Delay visit

blocks.note: first meaning: postpone
second meaning: remain somewhere as a guest for a while

explanation.surface: Put off a trip to someone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to hold back or suspend and to remain as a guest somewhere.

clue.text: Limestone country, well drained, ruggedly stark

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A stark, rugged limestone landscape where water drains away.
explanation.definitionFit: Karst is limestone terrain riddled with sinkholes and caves, through which water drains underground.

clue.text: Centre NE had redeveloped, given fresh allure

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: NE is the North East of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To reenchant is to charm again, so something reenchanted has been given renewed appeal.

clue.text: It's gathered at base of mountain to shelter, setting off north

definitions.text: It's gathered at base of mountain

indicators.note: setting something off means putting it aside, so that letter leaves

blocks.note: a screen gives shelter or cover
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Climbers gather at the foot of a mountain to take cover before heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: Scree is the loose broken rock that accumulates on slopes below a cliff or peak.

clue.text: Bearded condition after 'air grows wild

indicators.note: something growing wild is unruly and disordered, so its letters scramble

blocks.note: the word as written, dropped h and all, rearranged

explanation.surface: A cockney says a beard is what you get when your hair grows wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the condition after the rearranged letters. The apostrophe of 'air turns hair into a cockney pronunciation, adding to the beard picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristate, a botanical term, means having awns or bristles, so bearded in the plant sense.

clue.text: Renew power in alternative to stealth tax?

blocks.note: first meaning: top up a battery slowly and continuously
second meaning, whimsical: a levy that seeps out of you a little at a time

explanation.surface: A government proposes a new way to raise money instead of a hidden tax.
explanation.walkthrough: A stealth tax is one levied without being noticed; the question mark flags the fanciful reading of a charge that dribbles out gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: To trickle-charge a battery is to recharge it at a low steady rate; read literally, it is a fee taken in trickles.

clue.text: Mum's among threesome (not first time) in Greek dance

indicators.note: not first means the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: a troika is a group of three

a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Mother joins a trio for a Greek dance, though not for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not first time' means the T at the front is the letter dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The romaika is a Greek folk dance, named from the Romaic (modern Greek) people.

clue.text: Photo royalty? They're often slim

blocks.note: pic is informal for a picture or photo
kings are royalty

explanation.surface: A shot of the royals, followed by a remark that they're often thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slim pickings' is the idiom: scant gains or rewards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickings are the profits or spoils to be had, and in the stock phrase they are usually slim.

clue.text: Sweetly coated queen thoroughly enveloped in mixture of dyes

indicators.note: a mixture of letters has them blended into a new order
something enveloped in another is wrapped inside it

blocks.note: these letters rearranged, to be split around the inserted part
R for regina, Latin for queen
up means completely, as in eat up or use up

explanation.surface: A queen's portrait smothered in a blend of colours, sweetly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something syruped has been covered in syrup, a sweet sticky liquid.

clue.text: I can't die after treatment of glandular inflammation

indicators.note: after treatment something is altered, so the letters come out changed in order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient relieved after treatment declares they won't die of their swollen glands.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenitis is inflammation of a gland, and adenitic is its adjective, describing that condition.

clue.text: Chum in select year

blocks.note: to cull is to pick out or select
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A friend in a chosen year group at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Cully is an old slang word for a mate or companion, as well as a dupe.

clue.text: Saw tot with adult at bottom of street

blocks.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for street
to tot up is to add
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A toddler and a grown-up spotted at the end of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb but is the noun. In a down entry, the two pieces go at the bottom of the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadda is a double-bladed saw used by comb-makers, so a type of saw.

clue.text: Small child attached to nipple, a tiddler

blocks.note: tit is a word for a nipple or teat
CH is the abbreviation for child, 'small' signalling the short form

explanation.surface: A baby feeding at the breast is a little one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small child' looks like the definition but supplies the abbreviation; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Titch is British slang for a very small person, much as tiddler means a small child.

clue.text: Looped garland in honour of Indian prince

blocks.note: a dedication is to someone, in their honour
a rana is a Rajput prince in India

explanation.surface: A garland draped in tribute to a maharajah.
explanation.definitionFit: A torana is a festoon or looped garland hung over Indian doorways, and also a carved arched gateway.

clue.text: Mucker messed about in foul dirt (8, two words)

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: Mucker is British slang for a close friend, not someone who mucks about.
explanation.definitionFit: Old fruit is dated British slang for a chum, used affectionately like old chap or mucker.

clue.text: Dip, when entering river, well oiled

indicators.note: something entering another goes inside it

blocks.note: to dunk is to dip, as a biscuit in tea

explanation.surface: A tipsy swimmer takes a plunge into the river.

clue.text: Deck where you may see sailor all right

blocks.note: tar, short for tarpaulin, is a sailor

explanation.surface: On a ship's deck there is a sailor, and he is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' suggests a ship, fitting the sailor, but it is a deck of cards.

clue.text: Obscure area of land in old England

blocks.note: second meaning: an Anglo-Saxon land measure, enough to support a family

clue.text: They're first of Malaysian origin, resident overseas

clue.text: Stew inn cooked limits more than half greed

clue.text: Fit, Ron and Ted mostly wrestled at the same weight

taken as written with the final letter dropped

clue.text: Get rupture, return of old injury, being plastered

clue.text: Take leave to scan old holiday house once it's vacated
